item.title: Key figure in Sweden's Foxtrot gang seized in Iraq
item.description: A 21-year-old described by as "very close to the top leader" of the Foxtrot gang was arrested in Iraq in December, according to Swedish police.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: vovve
item.description: If you're raising bilingual children in Sweden, this may very well be one of their first words as soon as they start to get a sense of the world around them.

item.title: Calf dance and boiled bread: The Swedish foods with EU protection
item.description: Sweden is battling to win Norrland and East Coast Baltic herrings EU 'Protected Designation of Origin' status ‒ joining a stable of fishy specialities that is starting to rival France's list of cheeses. But a lot of the other specialities are pretty weird. How many of these have you heard of?

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Tuesday
item.description: Swedish customs make record cocaine haul, Leader of Swedish Armed Forces 'not worried about Nato's future', and other news from Sweden on Tuesday.

item.title: How Sweden's government ignored warnings when revoking 'track change law'
item.description: The Migration Agency warned it was moving too fast and the parliament's law-checking panel asked it to reconsider. But the government pushed ahead anyway, abolishing the track change law last April with retroactive effect.

item.title: How to enrol your child in a Swedish school
item.description: Is your child set to turn six this year? Then it’s time to start thinking about which school they’re going to attend.

item.title: Two-metre 'killer icicles' threaten Gothenburg pedestrians
item.description: Rescue services have warned people in Gothenburg to keep a look out for icicles up to two metres long and weighing up to 40kg, which have been identified hanging from roofs and gutters around the city.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: snögubbe
item.description: With much of Sweden below freezing – and a fair amount covered in snow – maybe this will give you some inspiration for what you can do while you're snowed in.

item.title: 'I’m not valued': The reasons foreign residents are leaving Sweden
item.description: The decision to bring in stricter citizenship rules is by far the chief factor pushing readers who answered our survey to leave Sweden, followed by problems integrating and socialising, slow permit processing times, and the high cost of living.

item.title: FACT CHECK: Will track changers really be able to return to Sweden after just 19 days?
item.description: Migration minister Johan Forssell has dismissed calls to reconsider abolishing the track changes law, saying that rejected applicants can just leave Sweden for 19 days and reapply. In reality the situation is far from that simple.
